title: acciddasuite
text: acciddasuite builds infectious disease forecasts steps: get_data() check_data(): fetch validate surveillance data. get_ncast() (optional): correct recent weeks reporting delays. get_cv() (optional): evaluate candidate models time series cross-validation. get_fcast(): ensemble best models forward-looking forecast. package relies fable modeling framework follows standard forecasting workflow described Hyndman & Athanasopoulos (2021). overall goal provide public health professionals easily-adoptable approach generating, evaluating forecasts, visualizing infectious disease forecasts. get information know whether forecasting best approach task, follow steps article.
code: library(acciddasuite)

title: acciddasuite
text: fetch weekly COVID-19 hospital admissions New York CDC NHSN via epidatr. Setting revisions = TRUE retrieves full revision history (.e. past versions data), needed nowcasting. can also provide data. Just pass check_data(). See vignette("external_data") formatting details.
code: df <- get_data(pathogen = "covid", geo_value = c("ny", "ca"), revisions = TRUE) tail(example_data) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   as_of      location target          target_end_date observation #>   <date>     <chr>    <chr>           <date>                <dbl> #> 1 2025-12-07 CA       wk inc flu hosp 2025-12-06              233 #> 2 2025-12-14 CA       wk inc flu hosp 2025-12-06              259 #> 3 2025-12-07 NY       wk inc flu hosp 2025-12-06             1160 #> 4 2025-12-14 NY       wk inc flu hosp 2025-12-06             1171 #> 5 2025-12-14 CA       wk inc flu hosp 2025-12-13              412 #> 6 2025-12-14 NY       wk inc flu hosp 2025-12-13             1462 df <- check_data(example_data) autoplot(df)

title: acciddasuite
text: recent weeks surveillance data almost always low hospitals still filing late reports (right truncated). feed raw counts forecaster, predictions biased downward. get_ncast() estimates recent counts look like reports arrive. default max_delay = 2, last 2 weeks corrected; everything left untouched.  corrected ncast$data contains two extra columns: ncast_lower ncast_upper (95% CrI) corrected weeks. get_fcast() detects automatically uses propagate nowcasting uncertainty final forecast.
code: ncast <- get_ncast(df) ncast #> <accidda_ncast> #> Target:   wk inc flu hosp #> Series:   2 (location) #> Window:   2022-06-04 to 2025-12-13 (7-day interval) #> Nowcast:  2025-12-06 to 2025-12-13 autoplot(ncast)

title: acciddasuite
text: Forecasting split two steps: get_cv() (model selection): time series cross-validation full (median corrected) series, starting eval_start_date. Models ranked WIS interval coverage. get_fcast() (final forecast): reuses ranking ensemble best top_n models projects h weeks future. nowcast columns present, forecast produced three baselines (lower, median, upper nowcast estimates) pooled, prediction intervals reflect model uncertainty nowcast uncertainty. set eval_start_date mark start evaluation window. observations date form initial training window, every series needs least two observations . Default models : NAIVE: Carries last observed value forward. simplest possible baseline. ETS (Exponential Smoothing): weighted average recent weeks matter older ones. Adapts trends seasonal patterns. THETA: Splits data long-term trend short-term fluctuations, forecasts separately, combines . ARIMA: Learns repeating patterns past values predict future ones. Auto-configured find best fit. can plot relative WIS model location autoplot(). value wis_relative_skill=1 indicates average performance, values 1 indicate lower WIS (better forecasts), values 1 indicate higher WIS (worse forecasts).  Plot ensemble forecast autoplot(fcast) (pass model = inspect single model instead):
code: eval_start_date <- as.Date("2024-01-10") cv <- get_cv(ncast, eval_start_date) cv #> <accidda_cv> #> Target:   wk inc flu hosp #> Series:   2 (location) #> Window:   2022-06-04 to 2025-12-13 (7-day interval) #> CV:       4 models x 25 origins (h = 4) autoplot(cv) fcast <- get_fcast(cv, top_n = 2) fcast #> <accidda_fcast> #> Target:   wk inc flu hosp #> Series:   2 (location) #> Forecast: 2025-12-20 to 2026-01-10 (h = 4) #> Models:   2 + ENSEMBLE autoplot(fcast)

title: acciddasuite
text: model compatible fable framework can passed get_cv() via models. Compose default_models() keep built-ins alongside :
code: library(fable) library(fable.prophet) library(EpiEstim) library(projections) my_models <- c(   default_models(),   list(     CUSTOM_ARIMA = ARIMA(observation ~ pdq(1, 1, 0)),     PROPHET = prophet(observation ~ season("year")),     NNETAR = NNETAR(observation),     EPIESTIM = EPIESTIM(observation, mean_si = 3, std_si = 2, rt_window = 7),     CHRONOS = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "chronos"),     TIMESFM = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "timesfm")   ) )  cv <- get_cv(   ncast,   eval_start_date = eval_start_date,   models = my_models )  fcast <- get_fcast(cv, top_n = 3)

title: Ebola 2026
text: May 2026, Democratic Republic Congo (DRC) reported Ebola outbreak, caused Bundibugyo strain, just five months previous epidemic. July 2026, 2,423 cases 967 deaths reported. Rapid forecasting essential guide public health response resource allocation. vignette demonstrates use acciddasuite forecast Ebola incidence using surveillance data Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB). vignette executed models computationally expensive. can run code machine, may take several minutes complete.

title: Ebola 2026
text: example ’ll model top 6 locations highest cumulative confirmed cases date. location build regular daily series running latest reporting date, carrying last cumulative count forward fill gaps enforcing counts never decrease (discarding downward corrections). also drop leading zeros location’s first case, since log transformation used models requires positive values, location whose outbreak started later simply begins shorter history.
code: library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(ggplot2)  ebola <- read.csv(   "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scc-usc/ebola2026/refs/heads/main/hubverse_observed_data.csv" ) |>   filter(     target == "insp_sitrep__cumulative_confirmed_cases__daily",     !is.na(location)   ) |>   mutate(target_end_date = as.Date(target_end_date))  top_locations <- ebola |>   slice_max(target_end_date, by = location) |>   slice_max(observation, n = 6) |>   pull(location)  common_end <- max(ebola$target_end_date)  ebola <- ebola |>   filter(location %in% top_locations) |>   arrange(location, target_end_date) |>   group_by(location) |>   complete(     target_end_date = seq(min(target_end_date), common_end, by = "day")   ) |>   fill(observation, .direction = "down") |> # carry cumulative over gaps   mutate(observation = cummax(coalesce(observation, 0))) |> # monotonic, per location   filter(cumsum(observation > 0) > 0) |> # drop pre-first-case zeros; log() needs > 0   ungroup() |>   mutate(target = "insp_sitrep__cumulative_confirmed_cases__daily")

title: Ebola 2026
text: check_data() validates Ebola data returns accidda_data object. function checks missing values, ensures data correct format, verifies necessary columns present. Revised history cumulative confirmed cases available outbreak, skip get_ncast() proceed directly cross-validation forecasting.
code: library(acciddasuite) data <- ebola |> check_data() data data |> autoplot()

title: Ebola 2026
text: get_cv() performs time series cross-validation data evaluate performance different forecasting models. use last 21 days data evaluation window. First define list models test. use default models provided acciddasuite fable add custom models, including ARIMA, (neural network), several foundation models. autoplot() summarises cross-validation performance using relative WIS (wis_relative_skill column cv$score). Raw WIS depends scale observed data therefore comparable across locations. Relative WIS removes scale dependence comparing models within location. location, models compared pairwise shared forecast targets using ratios mean WIS values. model’s relative skill geometric mean pairwise ratios. value wis_relative_skill=1 indicates average performance, values 1 indicate lower WIS (better forecasts), values 1 indicate higher WIS (worse forecasts). example, 0.8 corresponds 20% lower WIS typical competitor. log scale makes relative differences easier interpret: 0.5 2 represent half double average WIS, respectively, equally distant reference value 1. can also build summaries cv$score. example, raw WIS per model location.
code: library(fable) library(fable.prophet)  models <- c(   default_models(),   list(     CUSTOM_ARIMA = ARIMA(log(observation) ~ pdq(1, 1, 0)),     NNETAR = NNETAR(log(observation), n_networks = 10), # takes 5min     PROPHET = prophet(log(observation)),     # you will need a python environment (see reticulate)     CHRONOS = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "chronos"),     TIMESFM = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "timesfm"),     SUNDIAL = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "sundial"),     MOIRAI = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "moirai")   ) ) cv <- data |>   get_cv(     eval_start_date = max(data$data$target_end_date) - 21,     h = 7, # forecast 7 days ahead     models = models   ) cv cv |> autoplot() cv$score |>   group_by(location) |>   arrange(wis, .by_group = TRUE) |>   mutate(model_id_ordered = paste(model_id, location, sep = "__")) |>   ggplot(aes(y = reorder(model_id_ordered, wis), x = wis)) +   facet_wrap(~location, scales = "free") +   geom_col(aes(fill = model_id), show.legend = FALSE) +   scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) sub("__.*$", "", x)) +   theme_classic() +   labs(     title = "Cross-validation WIS by model and location",     x = "Weighted Interval Score (WIS)",     y = "Model"   )

title: Ebola 2026
text: default get_fcast() use best 3 model location based cross-validation results. function returns accidda_fcast object containing forecasts location. autoplot() visualizes ensemble forecasts location, including median, 50% 95% prediction intervals. can also build plot using as_tibble() extract forecast data ggplot2 create custom visualization.
code: fcast <- cv |> get_fcast() fcast fcast$meta$selection fcast |> autoplot() fcast |>   as_tibble() |>   ggplot() +   geom_ribbon(     aes(x = target_end_date, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = model_id),     alpha = 0.2,     show.legend = FALSE   ) +   geom_line(     aes(x = target_end_date, y = median, colour = model_id),     show.legend = TRUE   ) +   facet_wrap(~location, scales = "free") +   # ground truth   geom_line(     data = fcast$hub$oracle_output |>       filter(target_end_date >= as.Date("2026-07-01")),     aes(x = target_end_date, y = oracle_value),     color = "black"   ) +   theme_classic() +   theme(     legend.position = "bottom",     legend.title = element_blank()   )

title: EpiEstim model for fable — EPIESTIM
text: formula Response variable model, example observation. External predictors supported. mean_si Mean serial interval days. std_si Standard deviation serial interval days. rt_window Length sliding window (days) used estimate Rt. Smaller values respond quickly recent changes, larger values provide smoother estimates. Defaults 14. n_sim Number simulated forecast trajectories. Defaults 100. R_fix_within Logical indicating whether Rt held constant within simulated trajectory. Recommended short forecast horizons.

what: Forecast with a pretrained time-series model — FOUNDATION
title: Forecast with a pretrained time-series model — FOUNDATION
text: FOUNDATION() provides access large pretrained forecasting models within fable. Unlike traditional statistical models, models require training supplied data. fitting step stores observed history, forecasts generated directly pretrained model.

title: Forecast with a pretrained time-series model — FOUNDATION
code: FOUNDATION(   formula,   backend = c("chronos", "timesfm", "sundial", "moirai"),   model_id = NULL,   device = c("cpu", "cuda"),   n_samples = 200L )

title: Forecast with a pretrained time-series model — FOUNDATION
text: formula series forecast, example observation. count data, use log(observation) variance stabilisation required. fable automatically back-transforms forecasts. Additional predictors supported. backend Pretrained model backend use: "chronos", "timesfm", "sundial", "moirai". model_id Optional Hugging Face model identifier. NULL, default model selected backend used. device Computation device: "cpu" (default) "cuda". n_samples Number forecast samples generate. Defaults 200.

title: Forecast with a pretrained time-series model — FOUNDATION

title: Forecast with a pretrained time-series model — FOUNDATION
text: Forecasts returned format fable models, allowing used functions get_cv get_fcast. models run Python using reticulate. first forecast session, required Python dependencies model weights installed downloaded automatically. cached subsequent forecasts. Available models (backend): "chronos" Amazon Chronos. Default: amazon/chronos-t5-small. "timesfm" Google TimesFM. Default: google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch. "sundial" Tsinghua Sundial. Default: thuml/sundial-base-128m. "moirai" Salesforce Moirai. Default: Salesforce/moirai-1.1-R-small. models provide limited number quantiles, extreme prediction intervals may approximate.

title: Nowcast right-truncated surveillance data — get_ncast
text: Recent weeks surveillance data incomplete reporting delays (right truncation). get_ncast estimates final counts baselinenowcast, replacing last max_delay weeks every series leaving earlier weeks untouched. Downward revisions redistributed across earlier delays via preprocess_negative_values.

title: Nowcast right-truncated surveillance data — get_ncast
code: get_ncast(x, max_delay = 2, draws = 1000, prop_delay = 0.5, scale_factor = 3)

title: Nowcast right-truncated surveillance data — get_ncast
text: x accidda_data (get_data / check_data) revision history; use get_data(revisions = TRUE). max_delay Integer. Number recent weeks treated right-truncated. Default 2. draws Integer. Number posterior samples. Default 1000. prop_delay Numeric (0, 1). Proportion reference times used delay estimation. Default 0.5. scale_factor Numeric. Multiplier max_delay estimation window. Default 3.

title: Nowcast right-truncated surveillance data — get_ncast
text: accidda_ncast object shared backbone (key, target, window, interval, history) plus: data Corrected series. observation holds nowcast median corrected weeks; ncast_lower / ncast_upper (95\ propagate nowcast uncertainty. meta nowcast settings (max_delay, draws, prop_delay, scale_factor) ncast_summary, one tidy table per-series weekly nowcasts (median, CrI bounds reported--far observed count) plotted autoplot.
